A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe TR2M, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. V1 includes Appendix A.1–A.6; v2 ends after the references despite mentioning supplementary material. The omissions identified below concern the supplied v2.pdf, without assuming what an unavailable supplement contains.

before.justification: V1 reports original TR2M benchmark results, zero-shot evaluations, ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 reports TR2M benchmark results and ablations in Tables 1–5. Results retained from v1 still constitute original empirical outcomes of the work.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds image-level coarse contrast using pooled features ordered by fitted scale factors. Its loss is combined with the retained pixel-level contrast as L_soc = L_coarse + L_fine, substantially extending the training objective. The pixel-wise rescaling and pseudo-depth supervision pipeline remains.

E1.justification: The four training datasets and five zero-shot datasets remain the same. However, v1 Appendix A.4/Table 10 evaluates incorrect language descriptions from the same or a different domain; these distinct input-condition scenarios are absent from v2, narrowing reported test coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add UniK3D, UniDepth and DepthLM while removing AdaBins, NeWCRFs and ZeroDepth. Table 3 adds UniDepth-V-L and UniK3D-V-S/V-L comparisons. The appendix-only EndoDAC comparison is also absent from v2.

E3.justification: Tables 1–2 change Metric3Dv2's stated setting from domain adaptation to zero-shot while retaining its scores; this establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing a rerun. Table 3 adds small- and large-backbone UniK3D evaluations. TR2M's stated metrics, batch size, optimizer and 20-epoch training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 retains the main module and modality ablations but omits v1's SOC-on-NeWCRFs experiment, relative-depth backbone comparison, incorrect-description robustness tests, separate scale/shift ablation and depth-class sensitivity study (Tables 8–12). V1's t-SNE analysis is also absent. No reported ablation separately tests the newly added coarse contrastive term.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: The reported TR2M values in Tables 1–5 are unchanged, including NYUv2 AbsRel 0.082 and KITTI AbsRel 0.066. New comparator results substantially expand the main tables, and Table 3 changes TR2M's average rank from 1.4 to 2.40 under the expanded comparator set without changing its scores. V1's VOID/C3VD results and supplementary result entries in Tables 7–12 are absent from v2.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 7 formally defines scale-ordered image-level positive/negative pairs and their coarse contrastive objective. V1 Appendix A.3.2's closed-form least-squares derivation is absent, although the alignment optimization remains in the main text. These are localized mathematical changes; no theorem or proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim of lightweight, language-assisted pixel-wise transfer from relative to metric depth remains. The abstract and second contribution extend scale-oriented contrast to image and pixel levels, and the abstract adds an explicit claim about avoiding large metric-depth models and large training datasets.

C2.justification: V1's appendix discusses pseudo-supervision's accuracy tradeoff, caption overfitting, object-scale overfitting, unclear edges and vulnerability to erroneous descriptions; these qualifications are absent from v2. V2 adds an interpretation of coarse contrast as preserving scene-scale ordering and emphasizes data efficiency relative to newer metric-depth baselines.

D1.justification: V2 newly reports training-image counts, including 102K for TR2M, and states that there are 256 learnable scale embeddings. However, v1's detailed decoder/projector architecture, positivity transform, contrastive-key selection and caption-generation instructions are absent. Basic training hyperparameters, hardware and the code-access link remain.

R1.justification: The related-work structure and positioning against RSA largely persist. V2 adds citations to DepthLM, UniDepth, UniK3D and hybrid-grained language-guided depth estimation, while removing works including EndoDAC, MaskDINO and BLIP. The comparison narrative places greater emphasis on training-data efficiency relative to universal metric-depth models.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the wording remain. V2 introduces dual-level/coarse/fine terminology, condenses several background and results passages, rewrites the conclusion and adds contact information and acknowledgements. References to the appendix become references to supplementary material that is not included.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document to two columns, moves Figure 1 before the abstract, redraws the architecture and adds a dedicated dual-level contrast diagram. Tables 1–3 gain training-image columns and colored rankings, with new grouping headings in Tables 1–2. Existing qualitative examples are retained under new numbering, while the t-SNE display and appendix figures/tables are absent.

improvement.justification: The newer baselines and dedicated contrast diagram are useful additions. However, the supplied v2 loses implementation information needed for reproduction, substantial diagnostic evidence and explicit failure conditions documented in v1's appendix. It also expands the method with coarse contrast while retaining the existing TR2M scores and providing no ablation isolating that addition. The resulting loss of reproducibility and support for the revised contribution outweighs the improved baseline coverage.
